requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: When a predefined function is invoked, the number of actual parameters SHALL be the same as the number of formal parameters.
requirements.original: 1) the number of the actual parameters shall be the same as the number of the formal parameters; and

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: When a predefined function is invoked, each actual parameter SHALL evaluate to an element of the type of its corresponding formal parameter.
requirements.original: 2) each actual parameter shall evaluate to an element of its corresponding formal parameter's type; and

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: When a predefined function is invoked, every actual in and inout parameter SHALL be completely initialized, except as permitted for `lengthof`, `substr`, `replace`, `any2unistr`, `decvalue` and `decvalue_unichar`.
requirements.original: 3) all actual in and inout parameters shall be initialized with the following exceptions:

improper_terms.proper: actual parameters passed to in and inout formal parameters

ambiguity.issue: 'initialized' is contrasted with 'partially initialized' in the exceptions, so 'completely initialized' (glossary) is meant; 'actual in and inout parameters' means actual parameters for in/inout formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: Any actual parameter of the predefined functions `lengthof`, `substr` and `replace` MAY be partially initialized.
requirements.original: any parameters of the functions lengthof, substr and replace may be partially initialized;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter for the `invalue` formal parameter of the `any2unistr` predefined function MAY be uninitialized or partially initialized.
requirements.original: the invalue parameter of the any2unistr function may be uninitialized or partially initialized;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter for the `encoded_value` formal parameter of the `decvalue` and `decvalue_unichar` predefined functions MAY be uninitialized.
requirements.original: the encoded_value parameter of the decvalue and decvalue_unichar function may be uninitialized.

readings: Only `decvalue` and `decvalue_unichar` accept an uninitialized `encoded_value` actual parameter; for `decvalue_o` it SHALL be initialized.
`decvalue_o` (the octetstring variant, named `decvalue` in table 15) also accepts an uninitialized `encoded_value` actual parameter.
ambiguity.issue: `decvalue_o` is not listed although it has the same parameter structure; the literal reading (first) is used in canonical.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function MAY be defined within a module or be declared as an external function (`external`).
requirements.original: A function may be defined within a module or be declared as being defined externally (i.e. external).

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: An external function declaration has the syntax `external function` [`@deterministic` | `@control`] ExtFunctionIdentifier "(" [{(FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar) [","]}] ")" [`return` [TemplateModifier] Type].
requirements.original:
external function [ @deterministic | @control ] ExtFunctionIdentifier
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")"
  [ return [ TemplateModifier ] Type ]

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: The formal parameter list of an external function SHALL contain only value and template formal parameters (no timer or port formal parameters).
requirements.original:
external function [ @deterministic | @control ] ExtFunctionIdentifier
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")"
  [ return [ TemplateModifier ] Type ]

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: An external function declaration SHALL NOT contain a `runs on`, `mtc` or `system` clause.
requirements.original:
external function [ @deterministic | @control ] ExtFunctionIdentifier
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")"
  [ return [ TemplateModifier ] Type ]

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: An external function declaration SHALL NOT carry both the `@deterministic` and the `@control` modifier.
requirements.original:
external function [ @deterministic | @control ] ExtFunctionIdentifier
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")"
  [ return [ TemplateModifier ] Type ]

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: An external function declaration in a TTCN-3 module SHALL provide only the function interface (no statement block).
requirements.original: For an external function only the function interface has to be provided in the TTCN-3 module.

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: The realization of an external function IS outside the scope of the TTCN-3 core language standard.
requirements.original: The realization of the external function is outside the scope of the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: An external function MAY be declared deterministic by using the `@deterministic` modifier.
requirements.original: Using the @deterministic modifier, an external function can be declared to be deterministic.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-function
requirements.canonical: A deterministic external function IS safe to be called from the specific places listed in clause 16.1.4, where non-determinism could lead to unexpected side effects.
requirements.original: Deterministic functions are safe to be used when called from specific places where non-determinism could lead to unexpected side effects (see clause 16.1.4).

ambiguity.issue: The sentence speaks of 'deterministic functions' in general but appears in the external function clause; the glossary term 'deterministic function' is broader. Read as deterministic external functions.

requirements.subject: ent:control-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@control` modifier of an external function IS used in the same way as for functions, as described in clause 16.1.5.
requirements.original: The @control modifier is used in the same way as described in clause 16.1.5.

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: An external function SHOULD exchange information with the test system only via return values and parameter passing.
requirements.original: NOTE: External functions should only exchange information with the test system via return values and parameter passing.

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: An external function SHOULD NOT cause side effects that change the status of the test system and may influence the test outcome.
requirements.original: Side-effects that change the status of the test system and may influence the test outcome should be avoided.

requirements.subject: ent:side-effect
requirements.canonical: A side effect that changes the status of the test system CAN occur if an external function contains default handling, configuration, communication or timer operations.
requirements.original: Such side-effects can occur if an external function contains default handling, configuration, communication or timer operations.
